references.text: Introduces the laws concerning the sin offering and establishes the principle of unintentional sin (שְׁגָגָה) as the basis for this sacrifice
Parallel formulation regarding unintentional sin for an ordinary person from the people, using the same expression 'one of the Lord's commands that must not be done'
Elaborates on the concept of guilt (אָשֵׁם) when something is hidden from a person, with similar language about something being 'hidden' (נֶעְלַמ)
Supplementary law concerning the sin offering for the entire congregation of Israel when they sin unintentionally, using the same terminology 'the entire congregation of Israel'
Concerns the unintentional transgression of 'all these commands that the Lord has spoken,' parallel to 'one of the Lord's commands'
Israel sinned and broke the covenant, an example of collective sin where the whole congregation was held accountable
Refers to the offering for the people's unintentional sins (ἀγνοημάτων), linked to the arrangement in Leviticus regarding the sin offering for the congregation
